story_type: first crewed launch of a commercial spacecraft, booster lands on a ship
hook: Two astronauts on a rocket no one had ever ridden before.
narration: For the first time, NASA astronauts launched from American soil in a spacecraft built by a private company.
Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on May thirtieth, 2020, on a Falcon 9.
Just over a minute up, the rocket went supersonic. Soon they were pulling two point three times Earth's gravity.
[short pause] Then the first stage shut down and dropped away.
The booster flips around and lights three of its nine engines again to slow itself as it falls back into the atmosphere.
Nine minutes after launch, it landed on a drone ship. It was the first Falcon 9 ever to carry humans to orbit.
Up top, Bob and Doug were in orbit, moving at about sixteen thousand miles an hour.
outcome: Crew Dragon separated from its rocket and flew on toward the International Space Station.
title: First ride on a private spaceship
description:
NASA astronauts Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley launched on SpaceX's Crew Dragon from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, on May 30, 2020, the first time NASA astronauts flew from American soil in a commercially built spacecraft. The Falcon 9 booster landed on a drone ship.

facts.claim: First time NASA astronauts launched from American soil in a commercially built spacecraft; Behnken and Hurley, 3:22 p.m. May 30 from LC-39A at Kennedy
facts.source_quote: For the first time in history, NASA astronauts have launched from American soil in a commercially built and operated American crew spacecraft on its way to the International Space Station. The SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft carrying NASA astronauts Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley lifted off at 3:22 p.m. EDT, May 30th on the company’s Falcon 9 rocket from Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
